input: Learn to read a nutrition label properly

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Nutrition labels contain many components (calories, macros, micronutrients, % Daily Value, serving size, ingredients list, etc.) — knowing which parts to focus on changes how deep the plan needs to go.
Whether this is for the user personally, a family member, a client, or a class determines the tone, depth, and framing of the learning material.
The reason behind learning this — weight loss, managing a health condition, general wellness, helping a child, athletic performance — shapes which label elements matter most.
How much time the user can dedicate affects whether this is a quick 30-minute guide or a multi-day structured learning plan.
People learn differently — some prefer reading articles, others want videos, hands-on practice with real products, or a cheat sheet — this determines the format of resources recommended.
Knowing what 'done' looks like — e.g., being able to compare two products confidently, avoid certain ingredients, hit a macro target — defines the end goal and how to measure progress.
Whether the user wants to start learning right now with a simple framework, or build a longer study plan, determines the very first action step.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to read nutrition labels properly
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to develop the skill of correctly interpreting nutrition labels on food products.

questions.title: Which parts of the label matter most to you?
questions.description: Is the focus on calories only, macronutrients (protein/carbs/fat), micronutrients (vitamins/minerals), the ingredients list, % Daily Value, serving size, or all of it? This defines the scope of what to cover.

questions.title: Who are you learning this for?
questions.description: Is this for your own eating habits, for a family member (such as a child or elderly parent), for a client you are advising, or for a school or work project? This shapes the tone and framing.

questions.title: What is driving your interest in this right now?
questions.description: Is there a specific health goal or situation behind this — such as losing weight, managing diabetes, building muscle, avoiding allergens, or simply eating more mindfully? The motivation determines which label elements take priority.

questions.title: How much time can you give to this each day?
questions.description: Can you set aside a focused hour or two to learn this in one sitting, or would you prefer to absorb it in short 10-15 minute sessions spread over several days? This determines the pace and structure of the plan.

questions.title: How do you prefer to learn new information?
questions.description: Do you learn best by reading guides and articles, watching videos, following along with real food products in hand, using a quick reference cheat sheet, or a mix of these? This sets the format of recommended resources.

questions.title: What would confidently knowing this look like for you?
questions.description: What would success feel like — being able to compare two similar products and pick the better one, spot misleading health claims, hit a specific macro target, or avoid certain ingredients with ease? This defines the finish line.

questions.title: Do you want to start with real products or a framework first?
questions.description: Would you rather begin with a structured explanation of how labels work before applying it, or would you prefer to grab a product from your kitchen right now and learn by doing immediately? This determines the very first step.
